record.paper_title: Open Problems on Open Algebraic Varieties (Montreal 1994 Problems)
record.original_question: Let X be a smooth Q-acyclic surface of log-general type, and let (V,D) be a minimal simple-normal-crossings completion with X=V\D. Must the intersection number K_V·(K_V+D) equal 0?

evidence.quote: 1.4. CONJECTURE. For X, V, D as above KV (KV + D) = 0 .

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $X$ be a smooth complex algebraic surface that is $\mathbb{Q}$-acyclic (i.e., $H_i(X;\mathbb{Q})=0$ for all $i>0$) and of log-general type (i.e., the logarithmic Kodaira dimension $\bar{\kappa}(X)=2$). Let $(V,D)$ be a minimal smooth simple-normal-crossings completion of $X$, so that $V$ is a smooth projective surface, $D\subset V$ is a reduced simple normal crossings divisor, $X=V\setminus D$, and $(V,D)$ is minimal in the sense that no $(-1)$-curve in $V$ meets $D$ in at most one point transversally (so it cannot be contracted while preserving the SNC property). Let $K_V$ denote a canonical divisor of $V$.

Prove or disprove: under these hypotheses, the intersection number
$$K_V\cdot(K_V+D)=0.$$
artifact.status_search_result: Web searches did not yield a definitive resolution. The conjecture (that the logarithmic Chern number $K_V\cdot(K_V+D)$ vanishes for minimal SNC completions of smooth $\mathbb{Q}$-acyclic surfaces of log-general type) is part of the well-known Montreal 1994 problem list on open algebraic varieties. Subsequent work by Gurjar, Koras, Miyanishi, Russell, Zaidenberg and others has produced extensive structure theory for $\mathbb{Q}$-homology planes of log-general type, but no source surfaced in the search confirms a complete proof or counterexample to this particular intersection-number vanishing. Status is therefore reported as unknown.

status_evidence.title: Some recent results in the area of non-complete algebraic varieties
status_evidence.snippet: Survey of results on Q-homology planes, including those of log general type, by Miyanishi and collaborators.
status_evidence.claim: Surveys progress on Q-homology planes of log general type but does not clearly resolve the K_V(K_V+D)=0 conjecture.

status_evidence.title: On homology planes and contractible 4-manifolds
status_evidence.snippet: A homology plane of general type can have at worst a single cyclic quotient singularity (Gurjar, Koras, Miyanishi, Russell).
status_evidence.claim: Recent work continues to study homology planes of general type without indicating that the log Chern number vanishing conjecture is settled.
